div.head: Quadr Ded 29
div.ab: Genera causarum tria fuerant: Deliberatiuum, cuius modus duplex est: suasio et dissuasio (suasio tripliciter diuiditur: honesto, utili, possibili); in quo plus ualent spes et metus; demonstratiuum habebat duas species, laudem et uituperationem, quorum ordo trifariam distinguitur præsentibus, præteritis et futuris; tertium erat iudiciale, in quo de ipsius facti pena uel præmio sententia promulgatur.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 531 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

div.ab: The kinds of cases had been three: the deliberative, whose mode is twofold: persuasion and dissuasion (persuasion is divided threefold: by the honourable, the useful, the possible); in which hope and fear prevail most; the demonstrative had two species, praise and blame, whose order is distinguished threefold, by present, past and future things; the third was the judicial, in which sentence is pronounced on the punishment or reward of the deed itself.
